procubuisse: procumbō, -ere, -cubuī, -cubitum — to fall forward, sink down, lie prostrate (perf. inf.)
procubuit: prōcumbō, -ere, -cubuī, -cubitum — to lie down, sink down, stretch out (3rd sg. perf.)
proprium: proprius, -a, -um — one's own, lasting, peculiar (n. acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
pulsum: pellō, -ere, pepulī, pulsum — to drive, drive out (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg.)
pulsus: pellō, pellere, pepulī, pulsum — to drive, drive out, strike (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia) · also interrog. adj., n. nom. pl. (quae sint ea nūmina) · also exclam. adj., n. acc. pl. (quae bella exhausta canebat!; quae … regna) · also interrog. pron./adj., n. acc. pl., what? (quae quibus anteferam; quae … maiora) · also f. nom. pl. (quae … acies)
quaerendi: quaerō, -ere, quaesīvī, quaesītum — to seek (gerundive, m. nom. pl.: quaerendī reditūs, returns must be sought)
quando: quandō (conj.) — since; (adv.) when · also indef. adv. after sī, ever (sī quandō, if ever)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
qui: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. pron., m. nom. sg./pl.) · interrog. adj./pron., who? which? (m. nom. sg./pl.: Sed vos qui tandem) · also exclam. adj., what (youths)! (m. nom. pl.: Quī iuvenēs!)
quicquam: quisquam, quicquam — anyone, anything (n. nom./acc. sg., after a negative or sī)
quid: quis, quid — who, what (interrog., n. nom./acc. sg.) · also adverbially, why? (n. acc. sg.) · also indef. after sī, anything (n. nom./acc. sg.: sī quid) · also indef. after nē, anything (nē quid inexpertum)
quidem: quidem (adv.) — indeed, to be sure; at least
quin: quīn (adv., conj.) — nay more, indeed; why not (introducing an added point) · also (conj.) introducing a subjunctive clause after a negative, 'but that, without'
quisquam: quisquam, quicquam — anyone, anything (in questions and negatives) (nom. sg.)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.) · quis after sī — any(one) (indef., m. acc. pl.: sī quos)
rebusque: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, affair, matter; pl. circumstances (dat./abl. pl.) + -que, and
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also rēgia, -ae (f.), palace, royal house (nom. sg.: rēgia Pīcī)
rem: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter, deed (acc. sg.)
rettulit: referō, -ferre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, carry back, revive, tell (3rd sg. perf.)
robur: rōbur, rōboris (n.) — oak; hard timber (acc. sg.) · also nom. sg. (si rōbur … esset)
rumpitque: rumpō, -ere, rūpī, ruptum — to break, burst; vōcem rumpere, to burst out with speech (3rd sg. pres.) + -que 'and'
saeptus: saepiō, -īre, saepsī, saeptum — to enclose, wrap around (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
sanguine: sanguis, sanguinis (m.) — blood; descent, lineage (abl. sg.)
scilicet: scīlicet (adv.) — of course, doubtless, forsooth (often ironical)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sequetur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue; come after (3rd sg. fut., deponent)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sin: sin (conj.) — but if, if on the other hand
sinistros: sinister, -tra, -trum — left, on the left hand (m. acc. pl.)
siqua: sī + qua — if any, if in any way (indef. qua, f. nom. sg., with gloria) · also n. acc. pl. (siqua dona, any gifts)
sit: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
solido: solidus, -a, -um — solid, firm, whole (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
solitae: soleō, -ēre, solitus sum — to be accustomed, be wont; perf. part. (semi-deponent), f. nom. pl.
solitum: soleō, -ēre, solitus sum — to be accustomed; solitus, customary, usual (perf. part. as adj., n. nom./acc. sg.)
solum: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, soil, land (acc./nom. sg.); also sōlus, alone (n. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (sōlus, alone: hoc sōlum nōmen) · also adv., only, merely
stirpe: stirps, stirpis (f.) — stock, root, lineage (abl. sg.)
stragis: strāgēs, -is (f.) — slaughter, heap of slain, carnage (gen. sg.)
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
sumus: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st pl. pres.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
superbum: superbus, -a, -um — proud, haughty; splendid (m. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (Tibur superbum) · also n. acc. sg.
supersunt: supersum, -esse, -fuī — to remain, survive, be left over (3rd pl. pres.)
supplex: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, begging humbly (nom. sg.)
surgit: surgō, -ere, surrēxī, surrēctum — to rise, arise (3rd sg. pres.)
tale: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (n. acc. sg.; also n. nom. sg.)
talem: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f. acc. sg.)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tam: tam (adv.) — so, so much, to such a degree
tanta: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. abl. sg. (ex tantā urbe)
tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem)
tantumque: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (n. nom. sg., tantum nefas) + -que, and · also tantum, adv., so greatly, so much (n. acc. sg. as adv.)
tantus: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. sg.)
tartara: Tartarus, -ī (m.); pl. Tartara, -ōrum (n.) — the underworld, the nether depths (acc./nom. pl.)
tempestas: tempestās, tempestātis (f.) — storm, weather, season (nom. sg.)
temptare: temptō (tentō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to try, probe, test, attempt (pres. inf.)
temptat: temptō, -āre — to try, attempt, test (3rd sg. pres.)
territat: territō, -āre — to frighten, terrify (3rd sg. pres.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
teucrorum: Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Teucrians, Trojans (from Teucer, an early king of Troy) (gen. pl.)
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
totamque: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (f. acc. sg.) + -que, and
totiens: totiēns (adv.) — so often, so many times
tremescunt: tremescō, -ere — to begin to tremble, quake, shudder (3rd pl. pres.)
troia: Trōius, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (abl. sg., from Troy) · also nom. sg., Troy (servātaque serves Trōia fidem)
troianis: Trōiānus, -a, -um — Trojan, of Troy (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
tropaeis: tropaeum, -ī (n.) — trophy, memorial of victory (abl./dat. pl.)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) · also f. abl./dat. pl. (tuīs querēlīs)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumidum: tumidus, -a, -um — swollen, bloated, puffed up (m. acc. sg.)
tuorum: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.); tuōrum, of your people (m. gen. pl.)
turbare: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to throw into confusion, disturb (pres. inf. act.)
turne: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
tuto: tūtus, -a, -um — safe, secure (m./n. abl. sg.); also tūtō (adv.), safely
tydides: Tȳdīdēs, -ae (m.) — son of Tydeus, Diomedes (nom. sg., Greek patronymic)
ultra: ultrā (adv.) — beyond, further, more · also prep. + acc., beyond (vīrēs ultrā, beyond strength)
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
variisque: varius, -a, -um — various, manifold, different (f. abl. pl., with arboribus) + -que 'and' · also n. abl. pl. · also m. abl. pl.
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
veniamque: venia, -ae (f.) — favour, grace, indulgence (acc. sg.) + -que, and
venio: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (1st sg. pres.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
ventosa: ventōsus, -a, -um — windy, stormy, wind-swept (n. acc. pl.; ventōsa aequora)
verso: vertō, -ere, vertī, versum — to turn, turn round (perf. pass. part., m. abl. sg.)
veterum: vetus, veteris — old, ancient, long-standing (gen. pl.)
victae: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer; victa, conquered (perf. pass. part., f. nom. pl.; also f. gen./dat. sg.)
victoria: victōria, -ae (f.) — victory (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
videbit: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. fut.)
videmus: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (1st pl. pres.)
videret: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. impf. subj.)
vidimus: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see (1st pl. perf.)
vires: vīs (f.) — force; pl. vīrēs, strength (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (fractae vīrēs)
virtutis: virtūs, -ūtis (f.) — manly excellence, valour, courage (gen. sg.)
vis: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, power, violence; pl. vīrēs, strength (nom. sg.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres.: Vīs … vidēre?)
vivida: vīvidus, -a, -um — lively, vigorous, spirited (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
vocatis: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (perf. pass. part., m./f./n. abl. pl.) · also m. dat. pl. (patribus … vocātīs)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
vocet: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question) · also concessive subj. after quamvis (quamvis … vōcet)
volscorum: Volscī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Volscians, a people of Latium (gen. pl.)
